original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exhibit one rational rank-one solution of R+S+T+U=4I-E-F, for every pair of distinct old projectors, on which all four targets are subset sums, and record that this solution fails the inherited odd-c count.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the two-old length-6 support question left open by the one-old equation, for one explicit witness rather than a new alphabet.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. Support holds for this length-6 witness, but the witness fails the inherited odd-c count, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after one explicit six-label support witness and its odd-c count. Do not classify other solutions, and do not start the three-old length-7 equation.
evidence: Witness: A,B,P,Q,2A,2B are nonzero rank-one frames summing to 4I because P+Q=A+B=I. Every target is the corresponding projector pair. Every choice of two projectors as old calls leaves four rank-one added frames. Odd c detects P and Q only, against four targets. The inherited inequality is not reproved. This is one solution, not a census.

open_questions.question: Does any other solution of R+S+T+U=4I-E-F meet support and also have at least four labels of odd c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This witness meets support and fails the inherited odd-c count, so it is not a word. A different solution that meets both tests would be shorter than the eight-call minimum.
open_questions.first_step: Find one other integral solution with at least four odd-c labels and repeat the subset scan.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not classify the solutions of the length-6 equation.

open_questions.question: Can four added rank-one frames plus three old calls meet support at length 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Length 7 is the remaining once-each profile with four added frames. A word there would be shorter than the eight-call minimum.
open_questions.first_step: Fix three distinct projectors and the equation R+S+T+U=4I-E-F-G, then scan one rational rank-one solution.
open_questions.blocked_by: The six-label witness has no seventh matrix, and the length-6 subset sizes do not transfer.
